context: To decide whether to split an integer factor n in the maximum product problem, compare n with the product of the two pieces 2 and n - 2.
description: A gray bar at the top represents length n. A bar of equal length below has a short green piece labeled “2” on the left and a blue remainder labeled “n - 2” on the right. A vertical dashed line marks the cut. The conclusion below reads “For n ≥ 4, we always have 2(n - 2) ≥ n, so the final split should contain only factors of 1, 2, and 3.”

frames.explanation: Since 2(n - 2) - n = n - 4, the product stays the same at n = 4 and increases strictly for n > 4. Repeatedly splitting factors of at least 4 never reduces the product. Thus there is an optimal split using only 1, 2, and 3, although other optimal splits may retain a 4.
frames.title: Cutting can preserve or increase the product

summary: A large integer factor can be split again without reducing the product.
title: Cutting can preserve or increase the product
